proves: The code running on NEAR testnet is the code this repo builds: for each contract, base58 of sha256 of the local wasm equals the code_hash the chain reports, read with a public credential-free view_account call. Written because items was found running bytes this repo does not build — the A3 bug class, a fix that silently never reaches the chain, whose only clue is a deploy log line that looks like success. It FAILED on items the first time it ran, and passed after a redeploy. The three deployed contracts are now built with cargo near build reproducible-wasm inside a digest-pinned container from a named commit, so these hashes are a function of the committed source and not of this machine: anyone can run npm run build:reproducible on this commit and get the same bytes. The chain says which commit and which container, because NEP-330 build_info is populated where it read null before — which is what lets SourceScan and NearBlocks verify the contracts. The remaining limit, which the script prints itself: npm run build:contracts uses the local rustc and is deliberately NOT byte-stable, so comparing against that build proves nothing, and the failure message says so rather than leaving a reader to guess.
